speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if the pain is localized to one side or both wrists.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis).

The combination of recent camping in Minnesota, a history of self-resolving knee pain (likely early localized Lyme), and current monoarticular wrist pain with systemic symptoms like fever and chills is highly suggestive of disseminated Lyme disease. I am requesting joint aspiration of the left wrist and serological testing for Borrelia burgdorferi to confirm the diagnosis.
